works.candidateDecisionRationale: The full thesis is primarily a metatheoretical and philosophy-of-social-science inquiry into explanation in theories of Latin American popular habitat. Its research questions and objectives explicitly analyze logical organization and presuppositional content, especially ontology and epistemology; its theoretical construction is organized around Bungean systemism, Bhaskar's critical realism, Archer's structure-agency theory and mechanistic social explanation. The later urban empirical case validates the previously constructed metatheoretical/explanatory scheme rather than displacing that philosophical-conceptual research object. Under the strict humanities-only target, this work-specific disciplinary framing supports INCLUDE even though the program remains interdisciplinary REVIEW.

works.candidateDecisionRationale: The full thesis contains substantive humanities-facing interpretation of identity, collective imaginaries, appropriation, border culture and public meaning, using qualitative, hermeneutic and phenomenological elements. However, those dimensions are structurally inseparable from an urbanism/public-space research object: spatial configuration of Ciudad Juarez/El Paso, site and photographic analysis, public-space performance variables, accessibility/comfort/uses, surveys, and a final proposal of the border edge as a public-space typology. The full text therefore preserves the same genuine humanities/urbanism boundary seen at program level. Under a strict humanities-only target, the defensible work-specific judgment is to retain REVIEW rather than force INCLUDE or EXCLUDE.
